reviews.text: Run is a riveting rollercoaster ride from start to finish, pairing a pulse-pounding plot with powerhouse performances from Sarah Paulson and Kiera Allen.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: “Run” is a sneakily absorbing thriller that pokes at the idea of a mother’s domineering love and a child’s blind trust.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: You pretty much know where “Run” is going to go, but it gets there in the most entertaining way possible.
reviews.author: Dan Bayer

reviews.text: Just stylish and thoughtful enough to escape being cheap shlock. Instead, it's classy and enjoyable shlock.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: What could have been a throwaway piece of B-grade schlock is elevated to an A-grade armrest-clutcher thanks to a chilling premise, superb direction in the tradition of Alfred Hitchcock and a lead performance from Kiera Allen that is an absolute pearler.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Chaganty's career remains something worth keeping an eye on, even if this sophomore effort doesn't quite hit the highs of his debut.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: A minor anecdote that Chaganty takes to wild extremes, although always building with a firm hand a suspense with a credible and remarkably transmitted by Allen's omnipresent disengaged face. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ezequiel Boetti

reviews.text: The problem ... is Chaganty seems to earnestly believe he is making a serious thriller, refusing to acknowledge the vein of absurdity that runs through the entire thing.
reviews.author: Steven Warner

reviews.text: To a large extent, "Run" plays like gangbusters.
reviews.author: Jen Johans

reviews.text: Gets by almost entirely on the energies of its two lead actresses, including a beautifully villainous Sarah Paulson and newcomer Kiera Allen.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: Taut, compelling and with just the right scale and intensity to keep us engrossed without ever going too far over the top and collapsing into camp.
reviews.author: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas

reviews.text: Run starts off as a Horror movie, but quite soon it becomes clear that this is an A to Z Thriller flick. Halfway through audiences should probably turn up a notch their suspension of disbelief in order to keep enjoying this one.
reviews.author: Alejandro Turdó

reviews.text: ...Run sets up a Rear Window/Misery story of captivity and attempted break-out, but squanders almost all of the screen-time on admittedly engrossing physical detail...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Both leads are simply fantastic, and the simple premise unfolds with energy and intensity.
reviews.author: Scott Weinberg

reviews.text: Although it riffs on Stephen King's 'Misery' a great deal, 'Run' has enough genre thrills and chills going for it to make itself more than just a simple cover version.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: It's (Sarah Paulson's) American Horror Story pedigree which suggests there's more to this film than there really is.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: A problem with the film is its insistence to keep the characters mysterious.
reviews.author: Rahul Desai

reviews.text: "Run works as a compelling thriller because it casually reminds viewers that disability is a class that anyone can join. Whether by birth, accident or malice, anyone can become disabled, and so disability rights and concerns apply to everyone."
reviews.author: Cate Young

reviews.text: Another absorbing and effective thriller whose simple premise is executed with skill, good acting and no need for exposition. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Chaganty fully commits to delivering breathless thrills and outrageous revelations, rather than lecturing us about the real-world implications.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: Oozes tension and reveals that keep you nervously tapping the entire runtime.
reviews.author: Lindsay Traves

reviews.text: Chaganty has achieved great things with his second feature, which is a must-see for those who love a good adrenaline rush.
reviews.author: Alysha Prasad

reviews.text: A campy thriller that pits [a woman] against her disabled teenage daughter in a battle of wits that isn't quite sharp enough.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: Run is a subpar genre piece with good intentions if nothing else.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: While utterly predictable, Run keeps its head above water thanks to some nimble filmmaking and a great debut performance by Allen. After this latest use of Munchausen syndrome by proxy, though, it might be time to retire that storytelling device.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Clocking in at an economical 90 minutes, [Run] traverses through familiar beats, but its taut pacing and all-in performances elevate it well-above standard thriller fare.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: We marinate in the juiciest, briniest details and soak up the nail-biting, will-she-make-it moments.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: [A] worn path. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Miguel Romero Fernández

reviews.text: ... this murky domestic thriller provides fair entertainment, stepping up what was presented in 2018 with the disappointing Searching.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Run isn't a masterpiece, and the movie has some ideas that are recycled from other films, but it's a satisfying thriller for anyone intrigued by stories about one family member pitted against another.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Run is a worthy follow-up to Searching for Chaganty, a director who knows how to ratchet up the tension when it counts.
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: It's far from a terrible movie, but I'm not sure what the takeaway is meant to be.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Aneesh Chaganty crucially recognized the potential issue of having able-bodied filmmakers tell a disabled story.
reviews.author: Alicja Johnson

reviews.text: Paulson will be fine after this misstep. Ditto Allen, who could not be a more appealing lead or a resourceful damsel-in-distress.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: A quick-paced thriller that gets right to the action. There is high tension throughout that will have you on the edge of your seat, with great performances by the two leads.
reviews.author: Chauncey K. Robinson

reviews.text: An asphyxiating and twisted fun thriller. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: One of the most chilling things about Run is pondering just how many parents in the audience might sympathize with Diane a little and just how far into the movie they might get before that sympathy runs out.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: ...Run is one of those movies you recommend to friends...it feels like a personal discovery.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: This film is so achingly gorgeous that we don't want this party to end.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: I highly recommend checking it out. As long as you don't feel the need, like Chloe, to ask too many pesky questions.
reviews.author: Sara Stewart

reviews.text: Meat-and-potatoes thriller filmmaking of the first order.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: A couple of things elevate Run above the average.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: Dark domestic thriller has violence, mature themes.
reviews.author: JK Sooja

reviews.text: The cinematic equivalent of Babe Ruth calling his shot.
reviews.author: Enrique Acosta

reviews.text: Crisp cinematography by Hillary Spera, taut editing by Nick Johnson and Will Merrick, and quiet sound design create an environment where the creak of a floorboard or the click of a keyboard can set a new scare in motion.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: Sarah Paulson owns this role ... Chaganty delivers an effective, well-edited, and intense experience.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: It's a lean 90 minutes, and you want the experience to be over in the best of ways: it's almost too intense at points, and you need to take a breath.
reviews.author: Kimber Myers

reviews.text: Overall, Run is a pure thriller. It's energetic, suspenseful, and Paulson and Allen are forces to be reckoned with.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: Probably my favorite thriller that I've seen in recent memory.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: While it doesn't wholeheartedly embrace high camp, it certainly cozies up to the genre with some suspenseful set-pieces and a number of shots of Paulson dramatically nursing a glass of wine.
reviews.author: Kayleigh Donaldson

reviews.text: Even when you know where the story is going, Chaganty pulls the rug from under you and adds more mysteries.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: Run has a solid set-up, a talented cast and capable filmmakers behind the wheel. The problem is the movie's lack of interesting color and execution.
reviews.author: Jon Winkler

reviews.text: It oozes Stephen King vibes, intentionally, but stakes it's claim with a focus on mother/daughter dependency, and what can happen when one is too dependent on the other. Hell of a nice twist too.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: Strong performances distinguish this diverting, but mechanical thriller.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Chaganty and Ohanian's new film is an entwined illustration of that balance between show or tell.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: A couple of heart-pounding sequences of suspense and two terrific lead performances by Sarah Paulson and Kiera Allen are enough to keep Run moving, but its predictable twists end up kneecapping the film before it ever gets momentum.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: It's one of those thrillers that you enjoy like a cheeky Big Mac. It tastes good, but once you consume and settle, it's not that filling.
reviews.author: Daniel Hart

reviews.text: A simple premise executed with style, precision and efficiency. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Kiera Allen is astounding but the entire production feels imbalanced and rushed, favoring the horror in moments versus overall narrative cohesion.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Part Lifetime movie, part over-familiar Stephen King riff, Run is a silly but effective little thriller, its predictable twists enlivened by the powerhouse performances of its stars.
reviews.author: Joel Harley

reviews.text: An extremely effective edge of your seat thrill with a wildly impressive feature debut performance from Kiera Allen.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: Disabled representation is long overdue, and Run sets the standard by doing it right.
reviews.author: Chelsea Steiner

reviews.text: It's quick and clean - it comes in, does what it needs to do, and gets out before it overstays its welcome.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Run is a taut, well-constructed thriller...the sort of wild story that could easily have spiraled out-of-control, but even those moments that go bonkers high manage to reach the top without ever going over it.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: Run is a film so full of half-measures that you begin to wonder if it wouldn't be better off as Trot, or maybe Jog or Power Walk.
reviews.author: Sarah Gorr

reviews.text: Paulson's performance is what helps make this a wicked enjoyment in the tradition of classic paranoid thrillers.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Perhaps this is just the right breed of insidious thrills to engage you; it's certainly captivating.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Paulson's crazed manipulations are underserved by a narrative that collapses under the slightest scrutiny, and even a surprisingly nasty final scene can't fully make Run stand out from the steadily expanding Munchausen-syndrome-by-proxy subgenre.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: Sarah Paulson and Kierra Allen's on screen chemistry is incredible. Do yourself a favor and watch the three deleted scenes to help with unanswered questions and flow.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: With this sadistic, insidious portrayal, Sarah Paulson has become TV's malevolent angel-of-mercy - and newcomer Kiera Allen is a revelation.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: ...a top-tier thriller that stands head and shoulders above much of its similarly-themed brethren.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: A provocative escape thriller skillfully directed and paced by Aneesh Chaganty.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: While it doesn't bend the rules or invent any new ones, Run ticks all the boxes it needs to in surprising ways to come out on top.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: [Aneesh] Chaganty's taut direction helps and like "Searching", he knows well how to engage viewers with enough pathos that made us root for the main character.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Phenomenal acting intertwined within a thrilling screenplay!
reviews.author: Jason Escamilla

reviews.text: A perfectly paced, well-edited, and nimbly acted thriller.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: It's so small that it becomes thrilling. You're really right there with [Kiera Allen] as you're panicking.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: A brittle, nasty bit of fun.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: The third act doesn't withstand much logical scrutiny, but at least the film dispenses with much of the supernatural nonsense and visual gimmickry that tends to pervade genre films these days.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: I don't have anything bad to say about the production quality, and the acting was quite good.
reviews.author: Emma Wolfe

reviews.text: Sarah Paulson camps it up as a disconcerting woman smothering her daughter in the farfetched Hulu movie.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Watch this movie if you're looking for a fun ride, popcorn movie, and Sarah Paulson!
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: This fictive story ultimately goes in different directions. But it is an effectively pulse-quickening use of twisted parental need in the cause of movie suspense.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: There's plenty here that's entertaining, laugh-out-loud funny and lightly disturbing.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Don't be fooled, "Run" is just another riff on the "psycho mom" trope with no emotional insights into anyone or anything.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

reviews.text: This is a silly, ordinary thriller that never does anything to distinguish itself from countless predecessors, but it does have the benefit of a legitimately great performance from newcomer Kiera Allen.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: You'll be able to figure out where Run is headed pretty quickly, but that doesn't detract from the precise thrills and campy fun along the way.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Run gives its dual leads a slim window for making first impressions and finding bases for their roles, which makes their performances and Chaganty's direction doubly impressive.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: Run is a heart-pounding, Hitchcockian experience with a groundbreaking performance by Kiera Allen. Aneesh Chaganty's new thriller sets the standard for disability representation in film.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: Chaganty is actively expanding audiences' ideas of what movie heroes can be.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: It's not necessarily that the revelations will be all that shocking to jaded moviegoers; it's that we totally buy that they're revelations to her. It's a very promising debut.
reviews.author: Michael Ordoña

reviews.text: This is a tight, occasionally inventive, and surprisingly empowering thriller.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: It's a tight exercise in controlled chaos, simple in its suspense. Run toward it.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: A tale of survival intertwined with a story of abuse wrapped in the guise of a horror movie, Run executes its Misery-adjacent narrative with precision, occasional dark humour, and genuine terror.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Sarah Paulson is doing what she does best: being an unbridled force of nature who can deliver a deranged, captivating performance that gives you chills.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Though some of its subject matter may be familiar, the film is well handled throughout -- a satisfying slice of genre action with some serious subtext.
reviews.author: Jennie Kermode

reviews.text: With a stellar standout performance by [Kiera] Allen and an unforgettable performance by [Sarah] Paulson, Run is a film that will have you cheering for our heroine while trying to escape the terror of a deranged parent's love.
reviews.author: Shannon McGrew

reviews.text: Run isn't always a clever film, but it is a film in which the characters are clever, and it seems determined to avoid the kind of moments that leave you yelling at the screen in frustration about how terrible someone's choices are.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: The film holds together thanks to the superb performances from both Paulson and newcomer Allen.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Once the setup's been introduced, the tension continuously ratchets up until it finally reveals the most shocking of twists that you will not see coming.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: It's great fun, and not overly violent.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: A step down from the innovative Searching, but Run can entertain if you don't try too hard to think about the plot.
reviews.author: Joel Fisher

reviews.text: A nifty little thriller whose title pleads for an exclamation point.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: It's a familiar but enjoyably vindictive PG-13 thriller about mother/daughter trust issues. Plus a little psychopathology.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: It's good to see that there is no sophomore slump for Chaganty here, who has delivered a competent thriller once again.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: Pulling from Alfred Hitchcock, M. Night Shyamalan, Brian de Palma, and more, Run stitches together scenes from some of the best films.
reviews.author: Christopher James

reviews.text: Full of edge-of-your-seat, wickedly inventive, twisty-turn, shock-ya surprises, compounded by the irony of a protagonist not being able to do what the title suggests.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: Run is a breezy bit of entertainment that will give any genre fan about 90 minutes of cinematic pleasure.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: It's also a hell of a lot of fun on a basic B-movie level, thanks to Chaganty's expert control of tone, his superb crafting of suspense sequences, and excellent work from Paulson and Allen.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: Aneesh Chaganty's new thriller is taut, suspenseful, and unexpectedly tragic thanks to the lead performances.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: I'm a little bummed Run missed its opportunity to find a theatrical audience, because it's very much the kind of movie that would be fun to watch with others.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: It runs out of gas in the final act, but "Run" is quite the ride for its first hour.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Wielding strong performances from Paulson and Allen, Aneesh Chaganty's second feature film excels at building a thriller you won't get enough of.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: Run showcases the whiplash intensity and cold calculation of Sarah Paulson at her peak, with intense moments that will leave you breathless.
reviews.author: Jack Wilhelmi

reviews.text: A psychological thriller with frustratingly little to say about the trenches of the human mind, Run nevertheless satisfies as a taut and titillating get-out movie that lands somewhere between HBO's Sharp Objects and Whatever Happened To Baby Jane?
reviews.author: Beatrice Loayza

reviews.text: Gripping, engaging, incredibly gratifying, and led by two magnificent performances, 'Run' is the perfect cinematic treat to devour during lockdown.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Chaganty and Ohanian love ratcheting up the suspense within confined spaces, and they're really good at it.
reviews.author: G. Allen Johnson

reviews.text: [O]ne of the best and most surprising thrillers of the year.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: Sarah Paulson sends chills as an overprotective mother - to say the least - in a real American horror story. Excellent performances and sharp direction make it work.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: An effective little shocker that knows how to induce nail-biting anxiety.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Deftly filmed and edited, Run is undoubtedly effective on the small screen, but few other films this year have built and held tension this expertly, so as to be immediately worthy of a room full of people reacting in unison.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: I am extremely disappointed with the movie I watched. Not only is it predictable, but it's also rather comical in its exaggerated dialogue and storyline.
reviews.author: Natalie Zamora

reviews.text: Sarah Paulson is a master of providing us with terror, but it's Kiera Allen who steals the audience's attention.
reviews.author: Zofia Wijaszka

reviews.text: Sarah Paulson and Kiera Allen Are Equally Strong in Aneesh Chaganty's Relentless Thriller.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: An old-school thriller told expertly that refuses to let you settle, elevated by two excellent performances from Sarah Paulson and Kiera Allen.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: ...a moderate thrill ride that consistently keeps its pace.
reviews.author: Kimberley Elizabeth

reviews.text: Run doesn't reinvent the wheel but it doesn't have to. Allen makes a big impact in her first role and Chaganty once again proves to have a touch for making unexpected, groundbreaking, and entertaining thrillers.
reviews.author: Rosie Knight

reviews.text: The real meat of the plot gets underway in less than ten minutes, and stays on track for a lean, perfectly edited ninety minutes.
reviews.author: Gena Radcliffe

reviews.text: Both lead actresses are great, with the young Kiera Allen holding her own as the empathetic protagonist against Sarah Paulson's increasingly psychotic villain.
reviews.author: Reuben Baron

reviews.text: There's enough go-for-broke and whiplash-inducing shifts in tone on display to suggest this filmmaking duo has a future, even when their characters don't seem to have a past.
reviews.author: Ryan Lattanzio

reviews.text: Sarah Paulson, as usual, is the reason to watch this often thrilling, sometimes generic Hulu Original that keeps the Munchausen by Proxy subgenre alive and kicking.
reviews.author: Drew Tinnin

reviews.text: Run is a taut and highly suspenseful thriller that often zigs when you're expecting it to zag, resulting in an expertly crafted, nerve-shredding psychological thriller.
reviews.author: Heather Wixson

reviews.text: Yet again [director Aneesh Chaganty] shows that his license to thrill is bona-fide.
reviews.author: Nguyên Lê

reviews.text: Chaganty has a firm grasp on building Hitchcockian suspense and knows how to keep things moving along at breakneck speed. There are no real surprises in store, but that's okay. Even with a basic plot we've seen before, Run delivers on the thrills.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: Run is a satisfying thriller that, despite its formulaic nature, contains some interesting elements that reaffirms Aneesh Chaganty as a promising new voice in the industry.
reviews.author: Adam Patterson

reviews.text: The computer screen of Searching was a monumental achievement (especially when other films couldn't pull off that technique), but Chaganty proves he can find ways to turn everyday situations into nail biting suspense scenes.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: They've set a complex and nuanced trap with multiple layers ensuring every new discovery comes with another puzzle to solve. Every answer doubles as deflection.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Newcomer Allen holds her own throughout Run. opposite the gifted Paulson, adding another calculating villain to her rogues' gallery.
reviews.author: Michael Gingold

reviews.text: Dueling excellent performances from a deranged Sarah Paulson and spunky newcomer Kiera Allen (in her feature debut) make it hard to look away from the screen, not that the pacing of Geganty and Sev Ohanian's script allows much opportunity for distraction.
reviews.author: John DeFore

synopsis: An isolated teen discovers her mother's sinister secret.
